name: The Royal Crescent Hotel & Spa
positioning: Grade I listed Georgian hotel spanning two terraced houses in Bath's Royal Crescent, with an acre of gardens and a spa in a historic Georgian Bath House
best_for: Couples wanting individually decorated rooms, four-poster Deluxe Suites and a garden spa a short walk from Bath city centre
Families or groups who want the Family Suite or the Garden Villa with its own walled garden

facts.text: According to Condé Nast Traveler, the hotel spans a pair of Georgian terraced houses in Bath's Royal Crescent and is Grade I listed.
The hotel is a 5-minute walk from Bath city centre.
The hotel is a 2-minute walk from No. 1 Royal Crescent.
Each room and suite has individual décor.
Master Suites have panoramic views and intricate period features.
A dedicated Family Suite has twin rooms for children, a suite for the adults and a private conservatory.
The spa is in a historic Georgian Bath House.
Spa facilities include a pool, gym, sauna, steam room and hot tub.
Spa treatments use GROUND rituals and Medik8 skincare.
The restaurant, Montagu's Mews, uses fresh, locally sourced produce.
The hotel is dog-friendly, with space, beds and treats for dogs.

highlights.text: The hotel has a tranquil acre of gardens, an oasis of peace and privacy in the city.
The Garden Villa is a private residence with a walled garden and space for 8 guests.
According to Condé Nast Traveler, the spa pool is overlooked by chapel windows and has a door leading from the water out to the courtyard.
According to Condé Nast Traveler, in Jane Austen's Persuasion, Anne Elliot and Captain Wentworth confirm their relationship outside the front door of one of the Crescent's grand mansions.
The spa has an outdoor garden, where birdsong is the soundtrack.

considerations.text: Classic Rooms are at the rear of the building and overlook a neighbouring commercial area.
Heritage Rooms have views across the lawn, garden or city of Bath, though some have a more restricted outlook due to the building's historic architecture.
Condé Nast Traveler calls the spa surprisingly small for a spa hotel.
